description_ru: У одинокого старика уродилось столько яблок, что он раздаёт их соседям, и вся улица приходит к нему на праздник.
text:
Ivan is seventy years old. He lives alone in a small house at the end of Garden Street, and behind the house there is an old apple tree. His wife planted it forty years ago, and every autumn it gives him a few apples for a pie.

But this year is different.

One October morning, Ivan opens the back door and stops. The tree is full of apples, red and shiny, hundreds of them. Many are already on the grass. They lie there like little red lamps.

"What a year," he says. "What am I going to do with all of this?"

He takes a basket and starts to pick. After one hour he has three baskets, and the tree still looks full. He makes a pie, then another one, and then a third. By the evening the kitchen smells wonderful, but it also looks like a shop. There are apples on the table, on the chairs, and even on the television.

"Nobody can eat all this," Ivan says. "I need help."

The next morning he puts two baskets by the front gate with a small sign: FREE APPLES. PLEASE TAKE SOME.

At first nobody comes. Ivan watches from the window and drinks his tea. Then, at ten o'clock, a young woman with a baby stops at the gate.

"Are they really free?" she asks.

"Really," says Ivan, coming out. "Take as many as you like."

"Thank you so much! I make apple sauce for the baby." She takes six apples, and she smiles at him. "My name is Dana. I live in the blue house with the bicycle outside."

"I am Ivan."

By lunchtime both baskets are empty. Ivan fills them again. This time a man in a suit stops, then two schoolgirls, then an old woman who walks with a stick. Each of them says thank you, and each of them stays for a minute to talk. Ivan is surprised. In all those years on Garden Street, he never talked to so many people in one day.

The old woman, Mrs. Petrova, takes only one apple. "My teeth are not good," she says. "But the smell is wonderful."

"Then I bring you a pie," says Ivan, before he thinks about it. "Where do you live?"

"Number five. But you don't need to do that."

"I want to," he says, and it is true.

That afternoon he puts a hot pie in a dish and walks to number five. Mrs. Petrova opens the door in her slippers, and her face lights up. She asks him to come in, and they have tea and pie at her small table, and she tells him about her garden, her sons and the old days on the street. Ivan laughs more than he did all year.

When he goes home, he sees a plate on his doorstep with a cloth over it. Under the cloth there is a big, warm cake with nuts. A small note says: "From Dana, for the apples. P.S. My baby loves the sauce."

The next day brings more surprises. The man in the suit, who is called Mr. Lin, leaves a bottle of orange juice. The schoolgirls draw a picture of the tree and put it in his letterbox. Somebody brings a loaf of bread, and somebody else a jar of honey.

Ivan stands in his kitchen and looks at everything on the table. He is not sure what to say. He sits down, puts his hand over his eyes, and for a moment he is quiet.

His wife often said, "A tree is like a person, Ivan. It gives more when it feels loved." He never understood her then. Now, maybe, he does.

On Sunday, the last apples fall from the tree. Before he goes inside, Ivan hears a small voice.

"Mr. Ivan! Mr. Ivan!"

It is Dana, with her baby in a blue coat, and behind her, half the street. There are children with balloons, Mrs. Petrova with her stick, and Mr. Lin with a big pot of soup.

"We want to say thank you properly," says Dana. "Is it okay if we have a little party in your garden?"

Ivan opens his mouth, but no words come out. Then he says, "Please. Come in. I have a lot of pie."

Everybody laughs, and the little party starts. The children run around the tree and play hide and seek. Mrs. Petrova sits on a chair under the branches and holds the baby on her knee, and Ivan pours tea for everybody.

When it gets dark, the guests go home one by one, and the garden becomes quiet. Ivan stays outside for a while and looks at the empty tree.

"Thank you," he says to it softly. "See you next autumn."

Perhaps it is only the wind, but he thinks he can hear the branches whisper back.

focus_sounds.tip_ru: Рот открыт шире, чем для «э»; звук между «э» и «а».
Долгий «о» с округлёнными губами; тяните звук.
Кончик языка не касается нёба и не вибрирует; не раскатывайте русское «р».
Начните с «а» и плавно перейдите в «и»; не разделяйте на два звука.

questions.question: What does Ivan put by the gate?
questions.answer: Baskets with a sign: free apples.

questions.question: What do the neighbours give Ivan?
questions.answer: Cake, orange juice, bread, honey and a drawing.

questions.question: How does the story end?
questions.answer: The neighbours have a party in Ivan's garden.
